payload.analysis: Combined with suspected acute epididymo-orchitis, Doppler shows enlarged left testis, heterogeneous echo, enhanced vascularity, and retained blood flow, ruling out torsion. Elevated WBC and pus culture with P. aeruginosa confirm pyogenic infection; negative urinalysis and occult penis support primary scrotal infection. Tumor is unlikely given infectious findings. All key imaging and laboratory information is covered.

payload.report: The 13-year-old boy presents with left scrotal soreness and oedema for five days. Physical examination shows an enlarged testis and epididymis with purulent foci and no torsion. Laboratory tests reveal leukocytosis and Pseudomonas aeruginosa growth, strongly indicating a bacterial infection. Doppler ultrasound shows preserved blood flow and enhanced vascularity, supporting acute epididymo-orchitis while refuting testicular torsion and tumor. Negative urinalysis and occult penis favor a primary scrotal infection. Although a mild whirlpool sign raises minor concern for torsion, preserved perfusion and overwhelming infectious evidence make torsion and tumor unlikely. Thus the diagnosis is acute epididymo-orchitis.
